verifier_summaries: The researcher was careful about leaving places null, applied the show-plus-15 rule correctly, and handled the Golden Bridge gateway case well. Their sourcing was weaker than their notes suggest. (1) They labelled vietnamtourism.com as the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism, a government source. Its own legal page says it is an independent private travel media outlet with no government link, no named operator and unsigned articles. They relied on it for Cung An Định, Lăng Bác, Thiên Hậu, Làng hương, the Military History Museum and the Opera House. (2) Several values rest on templated or AI-style sites the rules exclude: offpeaktrip.com (no byline, boilerplate text), kupi.com (an image credited to "Kupi.com AI"), nomadotravel.app, travelsetu.com and nomads-travel-guide.com. (3) Three citations do not say what was claimed. The Traveloka page on Bến Thành gives no duration. The LocalVietnam page on Phu Văn Lâu calls it only a quick stop, with no 20-40 minute figure. The vietnamtourism.com Opera House page says 60-90 minutes, not 70 (VnExpress does confirm 70). (4) They missed some status changes. The HCMC Ho Chi Minh Museum at Nhà Rồng closed for renovation from 7 May 2026, and I found no confirmed reopening. Part of Công viên 23/9 has been fenced since late October 2026 for the Bến Thành–Cần Giờ rail station. Only the base and first level of Cột cờ are open to visitors. Snow Town's official website domain no longer resolves. (5) They described tiNiWorld Gigamall as a miniature world; it is a children's indoor playground chain. Of the 27 values they proposed, I accept 19 (some with small changes inside the agreement margin) and reject 8: FITO, Tiniworld Gigamall, Bến Thành, Vietopia, Bình Tây, the Da Nang Fine Arts Museum, the Hanoi HCM Museum and Cầu Mống. I agree with their null for all 42 null places, and I add status or category notes to 5 of them.

I accept 65 of the 69 entries and reject 4. I opened the cited sources for all 15 places where the researcher gave minutes, plus extra searches for the high-impact null places. Most quoted figures do match the page text, but the source quality is weaker than the researcher implies. (1) vietnamtourism.com is not a government site. Its legal notice calls it independent travel media with no tie to the national tourism authority, and its articles are unsigned. Six values rest wholly or partly on it, and the Women's Museum entry wrongly names it as the government body. (2) Nomado Travel is an unsigned guide with affiliate links. Three values that sit well above the category value rest on it alone: Ngọc Hoàng at 70, Helio at 120 and the HCMC History Museum at 120. I reject all three. The Nomado pagoda page even contradicts itself ("less than an hour" in its own text), and Frommer's gives one to two hours for the History Museum. (3) Two citations are wrong: the Headout Skydeck page gives no visit length (Civitatis lists 1 hour), and north-vietnam.com says 1-2 hours for Hỏa Lò, not 60-90 minutes. Neither changes the value. (4) The researcher missed three things: the 70-minute run time of Mơ Show at the Phú Thọ circus (Sài Gòn Giải Phóng), which gives 85 minutes; the summer-only season of the Hồ Tây water park; and the fact that Vin Gallery, like TomuraLee, is a gallery filed as a museum. The many null decisions were cautious and almost all sound. Category changes I back: TomuraLee and Vin Gallery to attraction.gallery, Kỳ Đài Quang Trung to food.street_food. I would not move Nhà hát Thành phố to performing arts, because daytime visitors see only the outside. TripAdvisor (403) and Trip.com (432) pages could not be opened, so those claims are unverified.
